subject: QBR readout prep: launch pace, roadmap status & delivery risks
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: QBR readout prep: launch pace, roadmap status & delivery risks

Team —

We need a concise, leadership-ready package for the QBR on Friday. Focus areas: roadmap status, actual launch timelines (what's gated vs. optimistic), and the top delivery risks with mitigations. Please do the following by EOD Thursday: 

- Marcus: update the timeline_master.xlsx with realistic cutover windows and mark any gating dependencies (infra, infra perf, security sign-off).
- Karthik: expand the launch_risk_register.csv to include probability/impact and an owner for each mitigation.
- Evelyn & Lauren: pull customer-impacting items and escalation history into the QBR_slides_draft_v1.pdf (slide 3 and 4).

Attachments: QBR_slides_draft_v1.pdf (draft), launch_risk_register.csv (v0.7), timeline_master.xlsx (v2). Also linking the shared Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/QBR-2027-Roadmap

Key asks from leadership: a single slide that summarizes 3 worst-case scenarios and the decision triggers (canary thresholds, rollback criteria, customer communication plan). If any of you cannot meet the ask by EOD Thursday, flag immediate blockers here so we can escalate.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 20:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: QBR readout prep: launch pace, roadmap status & delivery risks

Hannah —

Thanks. Quick status from Eng: updated timeline_master.xlsx attached (v2.1) — highlights below. Attachment: engineers_risk_notes.md (short-form notes).

Progress:
- Core serving runtime: daytime throughput target validated (internal perf tests stable at 1.2x baseline for seq=512), PRs for kernel selection landed.
- Canary infra: 2/3 canary clusters ready, we still need the third region to complete capacity tests (ETA Wed noon).

Top blockers (high priority):
1) Model pruning regressions — after quantization pass we see a 4–6% drop in accuracy on our reranking evals. Risk: customer-facing ranking quality during ramp. Mitigation: revert to unpruned variant for first rollout + run cold-cache A/B. Owner: Karthik.
2) Integration tests at scale — pod OOMs when hitting sustained burst traffic in east-us cluster. Risk: degraded latency during peak. Mitigation: temporary autoscale bump + patch kernel memory leak (PR ready, needs verification). Owner: Marcus.
3) Doc & onboarding for Dedicated customers lagging — will affect launch communications. Owner: Lauren.

I added probability/impact columns in launch_risk_register.csv and flagged the two highest-impact items. I can produce the three worst-case slides, but need the decision triggers from Product to finalize precise rollback thresholds (e.g., 95th p99 latency > 350ms for 5m).

Attaching: engineers_risk_notes.md (short notes), updated timeline_master.xlsx (v2.1).

— Marcus
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 02:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: QBR readout prep: launch pace, roadmap status & delivery risks

Marcus — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few notes and proposed mitigations.

On "Model pruning regressions":
- I can own a fast mitigation: revert the quantized model for the initial rollout (no pruning) and maintain the optimized variant behind a feature flag for beta customers. This buys us 2 weeks to re-run the quantization pipeline with a larger calibration set.
- Probability: medium (we saw the drop in two independent eval runs). Impact: high for customer UX.
- Owner: Karthik (mitigation), QA: Omar Diaz (cc'd in separate thread).

On "Integration tests / OOMs":
- Proposed short-term: increase pod memory to 48GB in east-us for the next 72h while we push a memory-fix branch. That requires ops approval (I will ping infra). Long-term: improved memory accounting in kernel selection (Q3 item).

Decision triggers (proposal for slides):
- Rollback: sustained p99 latency > 350ms for > 10 minutes AND error rate > 2% for external requests.
- Pause rollout: any customer-impacting rerank drift > 5% on the active eval set.

I'll update the launch_risk_register.csv with owners and the mitigation timelines by EOD Wed.

On Docs: happy to help with a concise integration note for Dedicated customers (Lauren/Evelyn, can you surface the top 3 customer-facing changes we should call out?).

On quoting previous mail:
> I can produce the three worst-case slides, but need the decision triggers from Product to finalize precise rollback thresholds

Consider the triggers above as a starting point.

— Karthik
Director, Engineering — Inference
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 09:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: QBR readout prep: launch pace, roadmap status & delivery risks

Hannah / team —

Quick clarification from a customer perspective: our procurement and cutover timeline is locked to a calendar window starting 2027-04-20; we need a firm go/no-go decision at least two weeks prior for internal approvals. Can you confirm whether the "optimistic" window in timeline_master.xlsx (late April) is still feasible if you adopt Karthik's revert strategy?

If you anticipate pushing beyond April, we need to know now so we can adjust our internal dependency workstreams. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if helpful.

Thanks — Sara
Head of Platform, Acme Corp
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: QBR readout prep: launch pace, roadmap status & delivery risks

Sara —

Thanks for flagging that external constraint. Short answer: with Karthik's proposed revert-to-unpruned variant and the temporary autoscale bump for east-us, we believe the late-April optimistic window remains feasible, but it is contingent on the perf regression fix and a green canary in the third region (ETA Wed noon).

Action items and owners to meet the customer deadline (target decision: 2027-04-06):
- Karthik: finalize revert plan and update launch_risk_register.csv (owner + mitigation dates) — due EOD Wed.
- Marcus: validate east-us autoscale patch and run a 2hr sustained load test on Thu — results in timeline_master.xlsx.
- Lauren / Evelyn: draft the customer comms and deployment note for Dedicated (first pass by Thu afternoon).

If any of these are at risk, call it out in this thread immediately so we can escalate and commit credits/extra run-time if needed. I'll schedule a 20m standup Thu 1600Z if everyone can make it — calendar invite to follow.

— Hannah
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
